name: MAX232
description: Dual EIA/TIA-232-F driver/receiver that lets a 5 V TTL/CMOS system talk to a true RS-232 line without a +/-12 V supply. An on-chip capacitive charge-pump (voltage doubler + inverter) generates the +/-RS-232 levels from a single 5 V rail using four external capacitors. It provides two transmit channels (TTL in, RS-232 out) and two receive channels (RS-232 in, TTL out), with +/-30 V input tolerance. The classic part for adding a 9-pin serial port to micros.

pins.name: C1+

pins.name: VS+
pins.description: regulated +RS-232 supply from charge pump (storage cap to GND); V+ on Maxim datasheet

pins.name: C1-
pins.description: negative terminal of charge-pump capacitor C1

pins.name: C2+

pins.name: C2-

pins.name: VS-
pins.description: regulated -RS-232 supply from charge pump (storage cap to GND); V- on Maxim datasheet

pins.name: T2OUT

pins.name: R2IN

pins.name: R1IN

pins.name: T1OUT

typical_application: Level-shift a microcontroller UART (TXD/RXD) to a DB9 RS-232 port for PC, modem, or instrument communication from a single 5 V rail.
gotchas: needs five external capacitors (C1-C4 charge-pump caps plus a reservoir cap) - it does not work standalone
MAX232 specifies 1 uF caps; MAX232A (and many clones) use 0.1 uF - wrong values compromise voltage levels or speed
only 2 TX + 2 RX channels, so a full hardware-handshake port (RTS/CTS/DTR/DSR) does not fit on one chip
data rate is limited (~120 kbit/s typ); not for high-speed serial
TI labels the charge-pump rails VS+ (pin 2) / VS- (pin 6); the original Maxim datasheet calls them V+ / V- - same pins
observe capacitor polarity and keep them close to the IC; long traces add ripple to the +/- rails
